notes:
Summary:
- Lampyrid builds an IDE-first developer platform (editor plugins + cloud CI) for distributed engineering teams. Interested in adding a code copilot that can stream completions and also call into secured tooling (run tests, lint, collect build logs) inside ephemeral sandboxes.

Key requirements (from CTO / platform lead):
- Must support safe function/tool calling: ability to trigger test runner, linters, and build tasks and capture exit codes/logs.
- Sandboxing: isolated ephemeral execution (containerized), strict resource limits, no uncontrolled outbound network. Prefer on-prem or VPC with optional air-gapped mode for enterprise customers.
- Low-latency streaming: IDE experience target is <=200ms initial token, sustained low tail latency for streaming logs.
- Model/version pinning: deterministic behavior across releases for reproducible refactors and CI checks.
- Audit & retention: full audit logs of action invocation, signed metadata, retention controls, KMS for secrets.
- Cost sensitivity: POC aims to evaluate cost per test-invocation vs current self-hosted runners.

Timeline / activities (CRM style):
- 2026-02-18: Intro call (AE: Eliot) — high level use case, asked about on-prem options.
- 2026-02-24: Deep-dive with platform eng (SE: Priya) — walked through function-calling API, security model. Fireflies: ff-20260224-vest-913.
- 2026-03-02: Shared PoC plan (drive link) and pricing ballpark.
- 2026-03-05: Engineering Q&A — asked about KV cache isolation and artifact cleanup.
- 2026-03-10: Internal security review kickoff; requested threat model and container hardening checklist.

PoC scope:
- Integrate Redwood function-calls to trigger unit-test harness inside ephemeral sandbox containers; stream stdout/stderr to IDE in real-time; capture logs to S3-compatible storage.
- Validate latency (initial token <200ms) and cost per invocation at expected concurrency (50 concurrent dev sessions).
- Demonstrate model pinning and rollback with a canary on a small % of developer traffic.

Quotes / paraphrases:
- CTO: "We can't let an LLM accidentally push or leak secrets — isolation and KMS are deal breakers."
- Lead Eng: "If we can stream build logs live and show failing test diffs inside the editor, adoption will skyrocket."

Technical notes / concerns:
- Needs fine-grained RBAC: who can invoke build/test flows and which repos are allowed.
- Artifact retention policy: engineering wants 30d default, legal wants 7y for certain clients. Need retention_controls.
- CI integration: must plug into their Jenkins/GitHub Actions runners and optionally replace some self-hosted agents.
- Prefer support for open models (quantized) and Redwood Optimize suggestions to reduce per-invocation cost.

Next steps / immediate actions:
- Redwood to deliver PoC checklist + hardened sandbox design doc by 2026-03-14 (assigned: Priya).
- Security sign-off meeting set for 2026-03-18 (attendees: Lampyrid security, Redwood security).
- AE to confirm procurement timeline and SOW details; forecast target 2026-06.

Attachments & refs: pricing + PoC plan (drive://redwood-deals/lampyrid/poc-plan-v2.pdf), pricing spreadsheet (drive://redwood-sales/pricing/lampyrid-pricing-2026-02-25.xlsx). Gmail thread: thread:1739a2d4-lampyrid-poc. Jira escalations: INF-5891 (performance tuning), SEC-2330 (sandbox hardening).
